question: A hollow pipe is 1.2 meters long and has an inner radius of 3 cm and outer radius of 4 cm. Find the volume of material used in the pipe.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert length to centimeters: 1.2 m = 120 cm.

Area of material cross-section = π × (Outer Radius² − Inner Radius²).

Difference in radius squares = 4² − 3² = 16 − 9 = 7.

Volume = 7 × 120 × π = 840π.

**∴ Answer = 840π cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the pipe (h) = 1.2 m = 120 cm

Inner radius (r) = 3 cm

Outer radius (R) = 4 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of material in a hollow pipe = π × (R² − r²) × h

 
 
 
• R=4 
• r=3 
• h = 120 cm Volume = π(R² − r²)h 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = π × (4² − 3²) × 120

⇒ Volume = π × (16 − 9) × 120

⇒ Volume = π × 7 × 120

⇒ Volume = 840π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
